notes: Modified cash basis village audit, same layout as FY2023. Governmental lines from the governmental funds Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances (p5 major funds, p6 Non-Major and Total Governmental Funds 2022 column). Taxes 186,612 split by Schedule 1 totals (p11: Property tax 100,160 + Motor vehicle tax 12,739 + Sales tax 73,713; nonmajor funds have no taxes); Intergovernmental revenues 97,744 split by p11 (Highway allocation 75,220 + Motor vehicle fees 5,467 + Homestead allocation 7,974 + Other 9,083). Grant proceeds 41,769: grantor not printed, category other / Grants. Bond proceeds 440,000 (Street fund) printed under Other financing sources -> debt_proceeds; Bond issue costs (8,360) -> other_financing. Beginning/ending cash = Total assets 2021/2022 of the governmental funds cash statement (p4: cash in bank + county treasurer, no investments); fund balances recorded separately (p6). Business-type from Exhibit H (modified cash; ties to Statement of Activities p2: charges 263,715, expenses 288,369, net position 178,688 -> 154,034); principal paid 70,000 is on the cash flow statement only. Proprietary cash flows from Exhibit I Totals 2022 (p9); noncapital financing printed 0. Balance sheet from the government-wide Statement of Net Position (p1) because it includes capital assets and debt. Detail: Schedule 1 per major fund (p10, totals p11), combining non-major schedule per fund (p12-13; Keno fund had no activity, balance 3,805), Exhibit H per proprietary fund (p8). Schedule 5 (p14, budget by fund group, totals only) and Schedule 6 (p15, proprietary totals budget basis) not recorded to avoid double counting. Read pages 1-15 of 15
